# fetchloom

fetchloom is uv for research data on windows, linux and macos, on x86_64 and arm64. `data.toml` lists the datasets, `data.lock` pins their files by SHA-256 and size, and one cache folder keeps each file once for every project. `fetchloom sync` fills `data/` by reflink, hardlink or copy.

## using fetchloom

- [front page](README.md): install and quick start
- [user guide](docs/user/README.md): every user page and when to read it
- [getting started](docs/user/getting-started.md): install from source until the first release, first project, restoring and undoing it
- [concepts](docs/user/concepts.md): manifest, lock, cache, placement, archives, webdataset shards and offline preparation
- [recipes](docs/user/recipes.md): datasets a command makes from others, declared with from, run, code and env, keyed by content, and reported as `build.needed` when they change
- [commands](docs/user/commands/README.md): command table, global options and terminal output
- [add](docs/user/commands/add.md): add and pin datasets, matching current references, a list of links with `-i`, or files on this machine pinned by their bytes with `ref = "local"`; recovery copies stay out of logs
- [sync](docs/user/commands/sync.md): restore pins, preserve local edits, sync named datasets alone and preview required repairs
- [build](docs/user/commands/build.md): `build --dry-run` shows each recipe step's command, what it reads and where its result goes, in order, and runs nothing; this version runs no step
- [lock](docs/user/commands/lock.md): check or upgrade pins without placement, and merge data.toml and data.lock offline after a git merge, with `--ours` and `--theirs` for datasets both sides changed
- [list](docs/user/commands/list.md): dataset references, locked sizes and folders, or one dataset's files; ctrl-c stops reading
- [export](docs/user/commands/export.md): SHA-256 lines for `sha256sum -c`, link lists and aria2c input files from the pins, complete or refused, with gaps named in JSON
- [search](docs/user/commands/search.md): concurrent public catalog search and explicit selection
- [status](docs/user/commands/status.md): local differences and success-with-differences behavior
- [path](docs/user/commands/path.md): absolute paths, an implicit sync of that dataset alone, `--locked` and the `result.path` JSON answer
- [remove](docs/user/commands/remove.md): remove entries and unchanged managed files
- [drop](docs/user/commands/drop.md): leave files out of a dataset for good, such as bad samples, as patterns in data.toml, offline; files inside an archive by its members table, files a source lists by exclude with data.lock rewritten
- [get](docs/user/commands/get.md): one-off downloads into a folder or, with `-o`, one checked file at a path that is never replaced without `--force`; batch folders, cancellable link lists with an optional SHA-256 a line and output-folder link rules
- [cache](docs/user/commands/cache.md): where the cache's space goes and what gc frees, exclusively locked garbage collection and verification; filesystem failures retain their causes
- [settings](docs/user/commands/settings.md): each setting's value and origin: variable, settings file, machine or default
- [auth](docs/user/commands/auth.md): signing in once, with keys shared with each source's own tools
- [completions](docs/user/commands/completions.md): shell completion scripts for bash, zsh, fish, powershell and elvish
- [sources](docs/user/sources/README.md): reference spellings, pins, credentials and limits for each family
- [URLs and DOIs](docs/user/sources/urls-and-dois.md): direct links, DOI handles routed to known sources, and raw github and gitlab file links
- [zenodo](docs/user/sources/zenodo.md): concrete record pins, checked source identity and re-resolution limits
- [figshare](docs/user/sources/figshare.md): article links, explicit versions, numeric titles, portal-page refusal and download restrictions
- [dataverse](docs/user/sources/dataverse.md): published dataset and file pins, explicit link versions and installation-scoped access
- [OSF](docs/user/sources/osf.md): osfstorage folders, file GUIDs and versioned download links
- [hugging face](docs/user/sources/hugging-face.md): repository revisions resolved to full commits, folder listings and gated access
- [kaggle](docs/user/sources/kaggle.md): dataset versions, kaggle DOIs and competition data with kaggle credentials
- [google drive](docs/user/sources/google-drive.md): shared files and folders, resource keys and download confirmation pages
- [dropbox](docs/user/sources/dropbox.md): shared file links and folder zips
- [cloud buckets](docs/user/sources/buckets.md): `s3://`, `s3:https://` and `gs://` prefixes, listing, version pins, and private S3 buckets read with AWS keys once `s3_buckets` lists them
- [data.toml](docs/user/reference/data-toml.md): manifest keys, path rules, `path = "."` for files straight in `data/`, shared folders and clashes, secret-URL rejection and credential-safe diagnostic citations
- [data.lock](docs/user/reference/data-lock.md): lock fields, extract and access, recipe results, source records and hash encodings
- [JSON output](docs/user/reference/json-output.md): schema, command results, serialization and stdout failures, partial cache failures and work counters
- [exit codes](docs/user/reference/exit-codes.md): stable error kinds and recovery decisions
- [environment](docs/user/reference/environment.md): runtime settings, credentials and color behavior
- [compatibility](docs/user/reference/compatibility.md): configured platform targets, the program each system uses for a `.rar` fetchloom leaves packed, terminals and build requirements
- [cache folder](docs/user/reference/cache-folder.md): shared cache layout, durable records, URL fingerprints and unreadable change-mark errors
- [project folder](docs/user/reference/project-folder.md): finding the project inside its git repository, owner records, placement state and metadata publication
- [scripting](docs/user/scripting.md): JSON recipes, conflict checks and the python helper
- [mirrors](docs/user/mirrors.md): folders and web servers that hold pinned files by SHA-256, asked before sources and checked before use; folders are read offline
- [CI](docs/user/ci.md): a cache kept between jobs and keyed on data.lock, recipes for github actions and gitlab, keys from CI secrets and exact-input checks
- [clusters](docs/user/hpc.md): home and scratch disks, many jobs, inode quotas and webdataset shards, offline compute nodes, shared-disk locks, one cache for a lab and backups that keep hardlinks
- [notebooks and containers](docs/user/notebooks.md): where the cache lasts on hosted notebooks, dev containers and codespaces, read-only roots, a kubernetes job and small disks
- [AI agents](docs/user/ai-agents.md): the agent skill, JSON contract and why there is no MCP server
- [agent skill](skills/fetchloom/SKILL.md): which command fits which task, safe flags and reading failures
- [windows](docs/user/windows.md): Defender, dev drives, aliases, synced folders and long paths
- [macos](docs/user/macos.md): cache location, apfs clones, icloud drive and cloud storage folders, unicode names
- [troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md): recorded errors, causes and fixes
- [limits](docs/user/limits.md): excluded workflows and reproducibility boundaries
